paper_a.title: Maximum Likelihood from Incomplete Data via the EM Algorithm

paper_b.title: A Maximization Technique Occurring in the Statistical Analysis of Probabilistic Functions of Markov Chains

pairs.why_related: Baum-Welch (1970) is the HMM-specific EM special case; DLR (1977) generalizes to arbitrary latent-variable models. Same E/M iteration, different communities.

paper_a.title: Classification and Regression Trees

paper_b.title: Induction of Decision Trees

pairs.why_related: Parallel development of recursive-partitioning classifiers using impurity-based splits. CART uses Gini + pruning; ID3 uses information gain. Independent communities (stats vs AI).

paper_a.title: Probability Inequalities for Sums of Bounded Random Variables

paper_b.title: A Measure of Asymptotic Efficiency for Tests of a Hypothesis Based on the Sum of Observations

pairs.why_related: Chernoff (1952) bounds Bernoulli/iid tail via MGF; Hoeffding (1963) generalizes to arbitrary bounded variables. Chernoff is a special case.

paper_a.title: A Theoretical Framework for Back-Propagation

paper_b.title: Learning Representations by Back-Propagating Errors

pairs.why_related: Chain-rule gradient computation for multilayer networks. Rumelhart popularized; LeCun's thesis framework gave Lagrangian/adjoint derivation. Arguably both rediscovered Werbos 1974.

paper_a.title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space

paper_b.title: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation

pairs.why_related: Both learn dense word embeddings via factorizations of co-occurrence statistics. word2vec does implicit PMI factorization (Levy-Goldberg); GloVe does explicit log-count factorization. Concurrent, aware.

paper_a.title: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes

paper_b.title: Stochastic Backpropagation and Approximate Inference in Deep Generative Models

pairs.why_related: Both derive the reparameterization trick and stochastic variational inference for continuous-latent deep generative models. Independent and roughly simultaneous.

paper_a.title: Generative Adversarial Nets

paper_b.title: Noise-Contrastive Estimation: A New Estimation Principle for Unnormalized Statistical Models

pairs.why_related: GANs can be viewed as NCE with a learned noise distribution (discriminator plays role of classifier between data and noise). Same underlying density-ratio estimation.

paper_a.title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization

paper_b.title: Lecture 6.5 - RMSProp: Divide the Gradient by a Running Average

pairs.why_related: Adam extends RMSProp by adding bias-corrected first-moment estimates (momentum) to the second-moment running average. RMSProp is Adam with beta_1=0 and no bias correction.

paper_a.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition

paper_b.title: Highway Networks

pairs.why_related: Both introduce skip/gating connections to enable training of very deep networks. Highway uses learned gates; ResNet uses identity shortcuts (special gate fixed to 1). Concurrent.

paper_a.title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training

paper_b.title: Layer Normalization

pairs.why_related: Same running-mean/variance normalization technique; LN normalizes across features within an example while BN normalizes across the batch. LN extends/adapts BN to RNNs.

paper_a.title: Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting

paper_b.title: Regularization of Neural Networks using DropConnect

pairs.why_related: Both inject multiplicative Bernoulli noise for regularization. Dropout masks activations; DropConnect masks weights (strict generalization). Same theoretical framework (model averaging).

paper_a.title: Attention Is All You Need

paper_b.title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate

pairs.why_related: Bahdanau introduced additive attention over encoder states; Transformer replaces RNN backbone with pure self-attention. Extension + architectural simplification.

paper_a.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers

paper_b.title: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training

pairs.why_related: Both pretrain Transformers on unlabeled text then fine-tune. GPT: left-to-right LM; BERT: masked LM (bidirectional). Concurrent, both from 2018.

paper_a.title: NeRF: Representing Scenes as Neural Radiance Fields

paper_b.title: Scene Representation Networks

pairs.why_related: Both learn implicit neural 3D scene representations from 2D views via differentiable rendering. SRN uses LSTM-based ray marching; NeRF uses volumetric rendering with positional encoding.

paper_a.title: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning

paper_b.title: Momentum Contrast for Unsupervised Visual Representation Learning

pairs.why_related: Both train encoders via InfoNCE contrastive loss on augmentations. MoCo uses momentum-updated memory bank; SimCLR uses large in-batch negatives. Concurrent.

paper_a.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models

paper_b.title: Score-Based Generative Modeling through SDEs
paper_b.authors: Song, Sohl-Dickstein, Kingma, Kumar, Ermon, Poole

pairs.why_related: Discrete-time DDPM and continuous-time score SDE are shown to be equivalent formulations of the same diffusion generative model. Independent then unified.

paper_a.title: Flow Matching for Generative Modeling

paper_b.title: Flow Straight and Fast: Learning to Generate and Transfer Data

pairs.why_related: Both learn ODE-based generative models by regressing on straight interpolation paths between noise and data. Nearly simultaneous (within 1 month).

paper_a.title: Mastering the Game of Go with Deep Neural Networks and Tree Search

paper_b.title: Temporal Difference Learning and TD-Gammon

pairs.why_related: Both combine neural-network value/policy estimation with TD-style self-play RL for two-player games. AlphaGo adds MCTS + policy network; same RL+NN template.

paper_a.title: Learning from Delayed Rewards (PhD thesis)

paper_b.title: On-Line Q-Learning Using Connectionist Systems

pairs.why_related: Off-policy Q-learning vs on-policy SARSA — same TD(0) update form with different choice of next-action. Classic contrast.

paper_a.title: Playing Atari with Deep Reinforcement Learning

paper_b.title: Neural Fitted Q Iteration

pairs.why_related: NFQ (2005) trains a NN on batch of Q-learning targets; DQN extends with experience replay + target network + online training on Atari.

paper_a.title: Asynchronous Methods for Deep RL

paper_b.title: Simple Statistical Gradient-Following Algorithms

pairs.why_related: A3C extends Williams' REINFORCE policy gradient with learned value baseline (advantage), parallel asynchronous workers, and deep NN function approximation.

paper_a.title: Proximal Policy Optimization

paper_b.title: Trust Region Policy Optimization

pairs.why_related: PPO replaces TRPO's hard KL trust-region constraint with a clipped surrogate loss; both are first-order approximations of natural-gradient policy updates. PPO strictly simpler.

paper_a.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning with Double Q-learning

paper_b.title: Human-level control through deep reinforcement learning

pairs.why_related: Double DQN fixes the positive-bias in the max operator of DQN by decoupling action-selection from evaluation using the target network, tightening the Q-value estimate.

paper_a.title: Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization

paper_b.title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization

pairs.why_related: AdamW fixes Adam's incorrect coupling of L2 regularization with adaptive per-parameter learning rates by decoupling weight decay from the gradient step. Same algorithm, corrected.

paper_a.title: Robust Stochastic Approximation Approach

paper_b.title: Stochastic First- and Zeroth-order Methods for Nonconvex Stochastic Programming

pairs.why_related: NJLS 2009 establishes optimal O(1/sqrt(k)) rate for convex SA. Ghadimi-Lan 2013 extends the same SA framework to nonconvex stochastic programming (RSG method), inheriting Lan's Lyapunov-style analysis.

paper_a.title: Problem Complexity and Method Efficiency

paper_b.title: The Relaxation Method of Finding the Common Point of Convex Sets

pairs.why_related: Mirror descent is equivalent to Bregman projected gradient; both define updates by minimizing a linear approximation plus Bregman divergence. Same algorithm, different names.

paper_a.title: A Dual Algorithm for the Solution of Nonlinear Variational Problems
paper_a.authors: Gabay, Mercier / Boyd et al. review

paper_b.title: On the Numerical Solution of Heat Conduction Problems

pairs.why_related: ADMM is Douglas-Rachford splitting applied to the dual of a composite optimization problem. Same fixed-point iteration in a different guise.

paper_a.title: An Algorithm for Quadratic Programming

paper_b.title: Matching Pursuits with Time-Frequency Dictionaries

pairs.why_related: Matching pursuit is Frank-Wolfe on the L1-ball (equivalently conditional gradient on atomic norms). Same greedy selection of extreme points.

paper_a.title: A Differential Equation for Modeling Nesterov's Accelerated Gradient Method: Theory and Insights

paper_b.title: Some Methods of Speeding Up the Convergence of Iteration Methods

pairs.why_related: Polyak (1964) introduces discrete heavy-ball momentum recurrence; Su-Boyd-Candes (2015) derives the continuous-time ODE limit of Nesterov-style momentum and explicitly contrasts it with Polyak's heavy-ball ODE.

paper_a.title: Accelerating Stochastic Gradient Descent using Predictive Variance Reduction

paper_b.title: A Stochastic Gradient Method with an Exponential Convergence Rate

pairs.why_related: Both achieve linear convergence for smooth strongly-convex finite-sum optimization via variance reduction. SAG stores per-example gradients; SVRG uses periodic full-gradient snapshots.

paper_a.title: SAGA: A Fast Incremental Gradient Method

paper_b.title: Accelerating Stochastic Gradient Descent using Predictive Variance Reduction

pairs.why_related: SAGA extends SVRG/SAG: unbiased gradient estimator (unlike SAG), no snapshot epoch (unlike SVRG), and handles proximal steps. Unifies and extends both.

paper_a.title: Total Generalized Variation

paper_b.title: Nonlinear Total Variation Based Noise Removal

pairs.why_related: TGV generalizes ROF's TV regularizer to higher-order derivatives to avoid staircase artifacts. ROF is TGV with only first-order term.

paper_a.title: Sampling Signals with Finite Rate of Innovation

pairs.why_related: Both recover structured sparse signals from sub-Nyquist samples. FRI uses Prony-like annihilating-filter; CS uses L1/RIP. Similar problem, very different machinery.

paper_a.title: Atomic Decomposition by Basis Pursuit

paper_b.title: Orthogonal Matching Pursuit

pairs.why_related: Sparse recovery via L1 (BP) vs greedy (OMP). OMP predates; BP frames recovery as convex program. Long rivalry in signal processing.

paper_a.title: Nonlinear Iterative Partial Least Squares

paper_b.title: Praktische Verfahren der Gleichungsaufloesung

pairs.why_related: NIPALS for the first principal component is algebraically identical to power iteration on the sample covariance. Rediscovered in chemometrics.

paper_a.title: Random Forests

paper_b.title: Bagging Predictors

pairs.why_related: Random Forests = bagging of decision trees + random feature subsampling at each split. Strict extension by same author.

paper_a.title: Bagging Predictors

paper_b.title: A Decision-Theoretic Generalization of On-Line Learning

pairs.why_related: Both are ensemble methods reducing variance/bias of weak learners. Bagging: bootstrap + average; Boosting: reweight examples sequentially. Developed in parallel.

paper_a.title: XGBoost: A Scalable Tree Boosting System

paper_b.title: Greedy Function Approximation: A Gradient Boosting Machine

pairs.why_related: XGBoost extends Friedman's GBM with second-order Taylor expansion, regularization, sparsity handling, and system-level optimizations. Strict extension.

paper_a.title: Visualizing Data using t-SNE

paper_b.title: UMAP: Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection

pairs.why_related: Both embed high-dim data to 2D/3D preserving neighborhood structure. t-SNE: KL on pairwise Gaussian/Student-t; UMAP: cross-entropy on fuzzy simplicial sets. Similar optimization, different theory.

paper_a.title: A Global Geometric Framework for Nonlinear Dimensionality Reduction

paper_b.title: Nonlinear Dimensionality Reduction by Locally Linear Embedding

pairs.why_related: Both embed manifolds into low-d Euclidean space; Isomap preserves geodesic distances (global), LLE preserves local linear reconstruction weights. Back-to-back Science 2000.

paper_a.title: Boosting Algorithms as Gradient Descent

paper_b.title: A Decision-Theoretic Generalization of On-Line Learning

pairs.why_related: Same AdaBoost algorithm re-derived as coordinate descent on exponential loss in function space. Alternative proof/interpretation.

paper_a.title: A Simple Adaptive Procedure Leading to Correlated Equilibrium

paper_b.title: Adaptive Game Playing Using Multiplicative Weights

pairs.why_related: Both achieve no-regret in repeated games via local update rules. Regret matching (econ) and MWU/Hedge (ML) are related but independent discoveries of no-regret dynamics.

paper_a.title: The Weighted Majority Algorithm

paper_b.title: Aggregating Strategies

pairs.why_related: Independent rediscovery of multiplicative weights for combining experts. Vovk (COLT'90) and Littlestone-Warmuth (Information&Computation 1994).

paper_a.title: A Theory of the Learnable

paper_b.title: On the Uniform Convergence of Relative Frequencies of Events

pairs.why_related: Both establish uniform convergence and sample complexity for learning binary concepts. VC (1971, russian stats) and Valiant (1984, CS): PAC recovers uniform convergence under VC dim.

paper_a.title: Local Rademacher Complexities

paper_b.title: Local Rademacher Complexities and Oracle Inequalities

pairs.why_related: Both develop localization for Rademacher bounds to get fast rates. BBM: Annals of Statistics 2005; Koltchinskii: Annals of Statistics 2006. Same bound, alternative proofs.

paper_a.title: Calibrating Noise to Sensitivity in Private Data Analysis

paper_b.title: What Can We Learn Privately?

pairs.why_related: DMNS (2006) defines central DP via Laplace mechanism; KLNRS (2008) defines local DP — the model where each user randomizes before sending. Local LDP is specialization/extension.

paper_a.title: Moser and Tardos Meet Lovasz

paper_b.title: A Constructive Proof of the General Lovasz Local Lemma

pairs.why_related: Kolipaka-Szegedy shows the MT algorithm converges up to Shearer's threshold (the true boundary of LLL), tightening MT's convergence range.

paper_a.title: Ergodic Behavior of Diagonal Measures

paper_b.title: On Sets of Integers Containing No k Elements in Arithmetic Progression

pairs.why_related: Same theorem (dense subsets of Z contain arbitrarily long APs) proved by two completely different methods: Szemeredi's combinatorial regularity lemma vs Furstenberg's ergodic correspondence.

paper_a.title: Regularity Lemma for k-Uniform Hypergraphs

paper_b.title: A New Proof of Szemeredi's Theorem

pairs.why_related: Both give new proofs of Szemeredi's theorem in the 2000s. Gowers: uniformity norms + Fourier; Rodl-Skokan/Tao/Gowers: hypergraph regularity. Distinct modern proofs.

paper_a.title: The Primes Contain Arbitrarily Long Arithmetic Progressions

paper_b.title: On Sets of Integers Containing No k Elements in Arithmetic Progression

pairs.why_related: Green-Tao transfers Szemeredi's theorem from positive-density subsets of Z to the primes (density zero) via a relative Szemeredi + pseudorandom majorant. Major extension.

paper_a.title: PRIMES is in P

paper_b.title: Riemann's Hypothesis and Tests for Primality

pairs.why_related: Both give polynomial-time primality tests; Miller assumes GRH (conditional); AKS is unconditional. Both leverage Fermat-style identities but very different reductions.

paper_a.title: Natural Proofs

paper_b.title: Lower Bounds on the Size of Bounded-Depth Networks

pairs.why_related: Natural Proofs (1997) abstractly characterizes the proof technique that Razborov (1987) and others had been using — formalizes the "largeness + constructivity" pattern as a barrier.

paper_a.title: A Simple Unpredictable Pseudo-Random Number Generator

paper_b.title: Theory and Application of Trapdoor Functions

pairs.why_related: Both construct cryptographic PRGs from hard problems. Yao: one-way permutations -> PRG; BBS: quadratic residuosity specific construction. Different but closely related.

paper_a.title: On Ideal Lattices and Learning With Errors Over Rings

paper_b.title: On Lattices Learning with Errors

pairs.why_related: Ring-LWE is the ideal-lattice specialization/extension of Regev's LWE, providing the same hardness guarantee with smaller keys via the ring structure of Z[x]/(f(x)).

paper_a.title: Fully Homomorphic Encryption Using Ideal Lattices

paper_b.title: Fully Homomorphic Encryption over the Integers

pairs.why_related: Both construct FHE by bootstrapping through a "somewhat homomorphic" scheme + squashing. Gentry: ideal lattices; DGHV: integers. Same framework, simpler instantiation.

paper_a.title: Fully Homomorphic Encryption without Bootstrapping

paper_b.title: Somewhat Practical Fully Homomorphic Encryption

pairs.why_related: Both construct leveled FHE from LWE without bootstrapping, differing in encoding (integer mod q vs plaintext mod t scale). Standard textbook equivalence.

paper_a.title: Communication-Efficient Learning of Deep Networks from Decentralized Data
paper_a.authors: McMahan, Moore, Ramage, Hampson, y Arcas

paper_b.title: Parallelized Stochastic Gradient Descent

pairs.why_related: FedAvg = Local SGD with non-IID worker data + periodic averaging. Rebranded and extended from earlier parallel SGD work; same algorithm, new motivation.

paper_a.title: Similarity Estimation Techniques from Rounding Algorithms

paper_b.title: Approximate Nearest Neighbors: Towards Removing the Curse of Dimensionality

pairs.why_related: SimHash is the LSH family for cosine similarity via random hyperplane rounding (from Goemans-Williamson MAX-CUT). Specialization of the general LSH framework.

paper_a.title: An Improved Data Stream Summary

paper_b.title: Space/Time Trade-offs in Hash Coding with Allowable Errors

pairs.why_related: Both use k hash functions into a compact array for approximate membership/count queries. Count-Min extends Bloom from Booleans to counts with different error guarantees (additive vs one-sided).

paper_a.title: HyperLogLog

paper_b.title: Probabilistic Counting Algorithms

pairs.why_related: HyperLogLog extends/refines Flajolet-Martin probabilistic distinct-counting with harmonic-mean estimator. Strict BI.

paper_a.title: Password Authentication with Insecure Communication

paper_b.title: A Digital Signature Based on a Conventional Encryption Function

pairs.why_related: Lamport one-time signature + Merkle tree combine to give Merkle signatures; hash chain is degenerate Merkle tree of depth n. Specialization.

paper_a.title: Polynomial-Time Algorithms for Prime Factorization

paper_b.title: On the Power of Quantum Computation

pairs.why_related: Shor's factoring algorithm explicitly extends Simon's hidden-subgroup algorithm from (Z/2)^n to Z/N^* using the quantum Fourier transform.

paper_a.title: A Fast Quantum Mechanical Algorithm

paper_b.title: Strengths and Weaknesses of Quantum Computing

pairs.why_related: Grover's algorithm achieves O(sqrt N) search; BBBV proves this is optimal (Omega(sqrt N) quantum query lower bound). Matching upper/lower bounds.

paper_a.title: Distribution of Eigenvalues for Some Sets of Random Matrices

paper_b.title: Characteristic Vectors of Bordered Matrices

pairs.why_related: Wigner: spectral density of symmetric Gaussian matrices (semicircle). Marchenko-Pastur: spectral density of sample covariance (free convolution of semicircle with Bernoulli). MP reduces to Wigner at c=1.

paper_a.title: Strong Convergence of the Empirical Distribution

paper_b.title: Convergence to the Semicircle Law

pairs.why_related: Both prove convergence of the empirical spectral distribution for sample covariance matrices using different Stieltjes-transform arguments.

paper_a.title: Limit Laws for Random Matrices and Free Products

pairs.why_related: Voiculescu's free probability unifies and extends classical RMT (Wigner, MP) by identifying the semicircle as free analogue of Gaussian and giving free-convolution calculus.

paper_a.title: Phase Transition of the Largest Eigenvalue

paper_b.title: On the Distribution of the Length of the Longest Increasing Subsequence

pairs.why_related: BBP extends BDJ's Tracy-Widom limit for top eigenvalue of Wishart to spiked covariance model, identifying the phase-transition threshold for largest eigenvalue.

paper_a.title: A Sequence of Approximated Solutions to the SK Model

paper_b.title: Solvable Model of a Spin-Glass

pairs.why_related: SK (1975) defines mean-field spin glass; Parisi (1980) provides its true free energy via replica-symmetry breaking. Proved correct by Talagrand (2006) / Guerra (2003).

paper_a.title: The Parisi Formula

paper_b.title: Broken Replica Symmetry Bounds in the Mean Field Spin Glass

pairs.why_related: Both prove the Parisi formula. Guerra gives the matching upper bound via interpolation; Talagrand gives the full proof via cavity method. Companion alternative proofs.

paper_a.title: A Bound for the Error in the Normal Approximation

paper_b.title: Eine neue Herleitung des Exponentialgesetzes

pairs.why_related: Both give quantitative CLT-type bounds. Lindeberg: classical replacement method; Stein: characterizing-operator approach yielding Berry-Esseen-type rates. Alternative proofs.

paper_a.title: Information-type measures of difference

paper_b.title: On Information and Sufficiency

pairs.why_related: Csiszar's f-divergence generalizes KL to arbitrary convex f. KL is f(t)=t log t; chi^2, TV, Hellinger are other instances. Strict generalization.

paper_a.title: Three Approaches to the Quantitative Definition of Information

paper_b.title: A Mathematical Theory of Communication

pairs.why_related: Both define measures of information. Shannon: statistical ensemble entropy; Kolmogorov: description-length of a single string. Related via Kolmogorov-Shannon coding theorem.

paper_a.title: A New Proof of Szemeredi's Theorem

paper_b.title: On Certain Sets of Integers

pairs.why_related: Gowers' U^k norms extend classical Fourier analysis (used by Roth for 3-APs) to nonlinear structures capturing k-APs. Extension.

paper_a.title: On Sets of Integers Which Contain No Three Terms

paper_b.title: On Certain Sets of Integers

pairs.why_related: Behrend (1946): lower bound construction for largest 3-AP-free subset of [N]. Roth (1953): matching upper bound Omega(N/log log N). Joint matching bounds.

paper_a.title: Lower Bounds of Tower Type for Szemeredi's Uniformity Lemma

paper_b.title: Regular Partitions of Graphs

pairs.why_related: Szemeredi's regularity lemma (1978) has tower-type complexity; Gowers (1997) shows this is tight. Matching upper/lower bounds (BI).

paper_a.title: Six Standard Deviations Suffice

paper_b.title: Problems and Results on 3-Chromatic Hypergraphs

pairs.why_related: Both use probabilistic method + entropy/compactness arguments to prove existence of combinatorial structures avoiding bad events. Spencer uses pigeonhole + partial coloring; LLL uses local independence.

paper_a.title: A Note on Hamiltonian Circuits

paper_b.title: On Maximal Paths and Circuits of Graphs

pairs.why_related: Both give sufficient conditions for graph Hamiltonicity via connectivity/independence. Erdos-Gallai: degree sequences; Chvatal-Erdos: connectivity + independence number.

paper_a.title: A Simple Proof of the Blowing-Up Lemma

paper_b.title: Information-type measures of difference (Csiszar)

pairs.why_related: Pinsker: ||P-Q||_TV^2 <= (1/2) D(P||Q). Marton: coupling proof via transportation cost giving W_2^2 <= 2 D(P||Q). Stronger (Wasserstein), implies Pinsker.

paper_a.title: Sur quelques points de la theorie des fonctions

pairs.why_related: Two formulations of compactness in R^n: sequential (every bounded sequence has convergent subsequence) vs covering (every open cover has finite subcover). Proved equivalent.

paper_a.title: A Generalization of Brouwer's Fixed Point Theorem

paper_b.title: Ueber Abbildung von Mannigfaltigkeiten

pairs.why_related: Kakutani extends Brouwer from continuous functions to upper-semicontinuous correspondences with convex values. Used by Nash for equilibrium existence.

paper_a.title: Equilibrium Points in N-Person Games

paper_b.title: Zur Theorie der Gesellschaftsspiele

pairs.why_related: von Neumann minimax: existence in 2-player zero-sum. Nash: extension to n-player general-sum via Kakutani. Strict generalization.

paper_a.title: Graphs and Matrices

paper_b.title: On Representatives of Subsets

pairs.why_related: Equivalent theorems: Koenig (bipartite max matching = min vertex cover) and Hall (SDR exists iff no defect). Dual LP formulations of the same polytope.

paper_a.title: Maximal Flow through a Network

paper_b.title: Zur allgemeinen Kurventheorie

pairs.why_related: Ford-Fulkerson max-flow/min-cut is the edge-capacitated generalization of Menger (vertex/edge connectivity = disjoint paths). Rediscovery + algorithmic extension.

paper_a.title: Reducibility Among Combinatorial Problems

paper_b.title: The Complexity of Theorem-Proving Procedures / Universal Search Problems

pairs.why_related: Cook (1971) and Levin (independently, 1973): SAT is NP-complete. Karp (1972) extends with 21 reductions to classical combinatorial problems. Classic SM + EXT.

paper_a.title: A New Polynomial-Time Algorithm for Linear Programming

paper_b.title: A Polynomial Algorithm in Linear Programming

pairs.why_related: Both polynomial-time LP algorithms. Khachiyan: ellipsoid (impractical); Karmarkar: projective interior-point (practical). Distinct machinery, same theorem (LP in P).

paper_a.title: Some Optimal Inapproximability Results

paper_b.title: Improved Approximation Algorithms for Maximum Cut

pairs.why_related: GW give 0.878 SDP approximation for MAX-CUT; Haastad + Khot-Kindler-Mossel-O'Donnell show 0.878 is tight assuming UGC. Matching upper/lower.

paper_a.title: On the Pricing of Corporate Debt

pairs.why_related: KMV is a commercial productization of Merton's structural credit model (equity as call option on firm value). Same mathematical model, different parameterization.

paper_a.title: The Pricing of Options and Corporate Liabilities

paper_b.title: Theory of Rational Option Pricing

pairs.why_related: Both derive European option pricing PDE in 1973. Black-Scholes: replication; Merton: continuous-time martingale / ito. Nearly simultaneous independent derivations.

paper_a.title: Common Risk Factors in the Returns on Stocks and Bonds

paper_b.title: The Arbitrage Theory of Capital Asset Pricing

pairs.why_related: Fama-French's empirical 3-factor model is an instance of Ross's theoretical APT (multi-factor linear asset pricing). FF identifies size and value as the relevant factors.

paper_a.title: A New Approach to Linear Filtering and Prediction

paper_b.title: Extrapolation, Interpolation, and Smoothing

pairs.why_related: Kalman (1960) recursive state-space linear filter is a specialization/reformulation of Wiener (1949) frequency-domain filter for stationary signals, extended to non-stationary via state.

paper_a.title: A Tutorial on Hidden Markov Models

paper_b.title: A New Approach to Linear Filtering and Prediction

pairs.why_related: HMM (discrete-state) and Kalman filter (linear-Gaussian continuous-state) are both instances of state-space models; forward-backward and Kalman recursions are the same sum-product on a chain.

paper_a.title: Error Bounds for Convolutional Codes

paper_b.title: On a Routing Problem

pairs.why_related: Viterbi algorithm for MAP sequence decoding is the tropical-semiring max-sum version of Bellman-Ford shortest path on a trellis graph. Same DP, different semirings.

paper_a.title: Factor Graphs and the Sum-Product Algorithm

paper_b.title: Probabilistic Reasoning in Intelligent Systems

pairs.why_related: Belief propagation on Bayesian networks (Pearl) and sum-product on factor graphs (KFL) are the same message-passing algorithm. Unifies BP, Viterbi, Kalman, FFT.

paper_a.title: Near Shannon Limit Error-Correcting Coding and Decoding

paper_b.title: Good Error-Correcting Codes Based on Very Sparse Matrices

pairs.why_related: Both approach Shannon limit via iterative decoding. Turbo (1993): parallel concatenated convolutional + MAP decoding. MacKay rediscovered Gallager's 1963 LDPC, showed iterative BP decoding. PR (turbo) + rediscovery (LDPC).

paper_a.title: Optimization by Simulated Annealing

paper_b.title: Equation of State Calculations by Fast Computing Machines

pairs.why_related: Simulated annealing extends Metropolis-Hastings sampling from fixed temperature to decreasing temperature schedule for optimization. Same accept/reject mechanism.

paper_a.title: Stochastic Relaxation, Gibbs Distributions

paper_b.title: Equation of State Calculations by Fast Computing Machines

pairs.why_related: Gibbs sampling is Metropolis-Hastings with conditional distribution as proposal (acceptance = 1). Strict specialization.

paper_a.title: Various Techniques Used in Connection with Random Digits

paper_b.title: Methods of Reducing Sample Size in Monte Carlo Computations

pairs.why_related: Two classical Monte Carlo variance-reduction/sampling schemes from the early 50s. Rejection: accept/reject; importance: reweight. Both target expectation under hard distribution.

paper_a.title: On Automatic Differentiation

paper_b.title: Learning Representations by Back-Propagating Errors

pairs.why_related: Backpropagation is reverse-mode automatic differentiation applied to a feedforward computation graph. Griewank's autodiff framework formalizes it in the general DAG setting.
